newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU scraps flour refund - officials.
newsitem.headline: EU scraps flour refund - officials.

text.p: The European Union has scrapped its standing wheat flour export refund of one Ecu per tonne after receiving bids through its daily channel for some 750,000 tonnes, member country officials said on Thursday.
The decision taken on Wednesday leaves the flour refund at a so-called dash, stripping of it numerical value and leaving any new licence holders exposed to a future tax.
The move also shortens the validity period.
Flour exporters, seizing on the possible fresh disappearance of export subsidies for wheat grain, bid heavily for flour licences at one Ecu between Friday and Tuesday, traders said.
The licences are delivered on a first-come, first-served basis, although the European Commission has a power of veto lasting three working days.

Abolishing the flour refund and withdrawing prefixation is designed to slow down the traffic and also gives the Commission more room for manoeuvre in sorting out bids for wheat grain exports, which are now split between taxes and refunds.

Grain sources said the EU may also have found it difficult to tackle complaints by U.S. millers, already hit by the rising dollar, had it reverted to taxing wheat grain while leaving its flour millers with a subsidised edge in the world market.
A French miller said the previous flour refund of one Ecu per tonne reflected the industry's needs, and exporters had been able to cover immediate needs and take some long positions.

"With one Ecu refund, and the dollar going up, this was a good level for millers who were short in July. So the volume of bids was not unusual," the miller said, putting the total of flour licences booked at 750,000 tonnes.
